headline: NQ compresses into the middle of an unchanged 102-point overnight band, leaving mean reversion intact below Monday's record Nasdaq-100 cash close
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,362.00, up 44.25 points (+0.14%) from the 31,317.75 previous close. Price sits 52.75 points above the 31,309.25 overnight low and 49.25 below the 31,411.25 Globex high, within two points of the exact midpoint of a 102.00-point band worth about 0.33% of index value. The decisive observation for the Tail score is that the band itself is unchanged from the previous assessment an hour ago: no new high and no new low were set, and price drifted roughly seven points. An hour of range compression around the midpoint, after the earlier push to the Globex high was given back, is working mean reversion rather than the persistent no-retracement path this score exists to detect, so Tail eases to 8%. E-mini S&P 500 futures confirm it at 7,835.25 in a 9.50-point range, and VIX at 15.52 against a 15.31 prior close shows no bid for protection. The Asian handover offers no aligned directional lead either, with the Nikkei up 0.3% and the Hang Seng up 0.8% against a 0.8% fall in Korea, and the Bank of Japan governor's scheduled remarks are a checkpoint whose transmission to NQ runs through yields and the yen rather than directly. The backdrop is genuinely strong: the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 31,076.44, up 268.51 points (+0.87%), in a 30,798.42-31,117.36 range, led by semiconductors as Nvidia pushed toward a 6 trillion dollar valuation on an expanded buyback and an analyst upgrade. That record close is context for what an opening auction may test later today, not evidence of present structure, and the published forecast treats it as a conditional checkpoint at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC. The live concern remains in fixed income. The 10-year yield stands at 5.31%, up from a 5.28% prior close and the highest since 2007, against H.15 readings of 4.83% at two years and 5.63% at thirty years, and market commentary has explicitly flagged that bonds and equities are pricing very different outcomes while indexes sit near records. Brent near 100 dollars with WTI at 89.87 keeps energy an inflation input, though Aramco price cuts and Hormuz crude flows recovering to 76% of prewar levels point toward de-escalation rather than a new amplifier, and gold at 4,152.00 is marginally lower. None of that has transmitted into a one-way index path, so it is carried in Stress at 45% rather than in Tail. Confidence is 86%: current futures levels and ranges, the cash close, VIX, the 10-year yield, the H.15 curve, oil, gold, the Asian session and a verified seven-day U.S. calendar were gathered directly from primary sources this run, with the shared Finviz context file the one input unavailable because its latest collection is roughly seven days stale and its calendar and futures sections failed outright, so it was excluded as supporting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour on 5 October, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 8% in the Asian session down to 6% at 08:00 UTC, climbed through the European and U.S. sessions to that 20% peak, then decayed to 9% by 00:00 UTC, printed 12% at 01:00 UTC on a new Globex high and settled between 9% and 10% through 04:00 UTC. Stress fell steadily from 54% to 45% as realised volatility compressed even while long-end yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 86% and 89% throughout. The 06:00 UTC hour on 5 October has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds at 8-10% through the thin late-Asian and pre-European hours, steps up from the European cash open at 08:00 UTC, peaks at 20% across the first two U.S. cash hours, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 17% reading in the power hour before easing to 10% by the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 45% and 54%, and Confidence declines from 86% to 77% as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path has been observed at assessment time, and the scheduled items in the event calendar are checkpoints rather than assertions about outcomes. The 10-year auction and the FOMC minutes fall on 7 October, after this window closes.
